cases.situation: New downstairs neighbour smokes on his balcony every night around 10 and it comes straight into our bedroom window. Never met him. Building rules allow balcony smoking.
cases.reply: Hi, I'm Aisha from 4B, right above you, and welcome to the building! I'm not sure you'd know, but smoke from your balcony drifts straight up into our bedroom window, mostly around 10pm. Would you mind using the far end by the railing in the evenings? Thanks, and let me know if anything from our side ever bothers you too.
cases.note: Smoking is allowed here, so ask for something he can easily do rather than asking him to stop.

cases.situation: El perro del vecino de al lado ladra casi todo el día cuando ellos trabajan. Hablé con él, Javier, a finales de agosto y sigue igual. Yo trabajo desde casa.
cases.reply: Hola, Javier. Te escribo otra vez por lo de Toby. Desde que hablamos el 28 de agosto sigue ladrando mucho entre semana; lo tengo apuntado, por ejemplo el 15, el 22 y el 24 de septiembre, más de dos horas seguidas por la mañana. ¿Os ayudaría que alguien lo sacara a pasear a mediodía? Prefiero que lo arreglemos entre nosotros, pero si sigue así lo comentaré en el ayuntamiento.
cases.note: Fechas del registro en vez de «todo el día», y el siguiente paso se anuncia antes de darlo.

cases.situation: Knocked on my neighbour Greg's door about his contractor's van blocking our shared driveway every morning. He got angry and said I'm 'always complaining'. Want to follow up in writing a few days later.
cases.reply: Hi Greg, our chat on Monday landed badly and that wasn't my aim. The only thing I'm asking is that the van isn't parked across the shared driveway before 8:15, so I can get the kids to school. Could the crew park on the street in front of yours in the mornings? Happy to talk whenever suits you.
cases.note: Don't argue the 'always complaining' point. Shrink the ask to one time window; if it continues, tell him before you go to anyone else.
